question.text: About 40 members of the Parliament in the UK represent this country, home to the cities of Gwynedd and Swansea.
question.clue: An independence struggle in this region was led by Owen Glendower.

swap.leadin: The Cavalier poets were so called because they supported this leader in the English Civil War.
swap.text: Name this son of James I, who was disliked by his country's legislature. He was executed after the English Civil War.
swap.clue: This ruler was depicted "at the hunt" by his court painter, Anthony van Dyck.

question.text: This victorious Norman leader at Hastings was the cousin of Edward the Confessor.
question.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I of England or Duke William II of Normandy; accept William the Bastard]
question.clue: This man received a blessing from Pope Alexander II to perform his most famous action, which he claimed was sanctioned by Edward the Confessor.

swap.leadin: Identify some figures related to the Napoleonic Wars.
swap.text: This English commander got lucky at the Battle of Waterloo and was twice Prime Minister but was unable to prevent the passage of the Reform Bill of 1832 and was named Field Marshal after the Peninsular Campaign.
swap.clue: This general defeated Marshals Jourdan and Marmont at Vitoria and Salamanca, and he replaced Lord Castlereagh as British representative to the Congress of Vienna.

question.leadin: Sir William Stanley's reinforcements turned the tide of this battle.
question.text: Name this 1485 battle, during which forces under the future Henry VII defeated Richard III.
question.clue: The leader of the losing army managed to unhorse John Cheyne and kill Sir William Brandon, but failed to receive assistance from Henry Percy's reserves.

swap.leadin: He served as Chancellor of the Exchequer under Lord Derby.
swap.text: Name this Jewish Prime Minister who also led the Young England movement.
swap.clue: This leader wrote about the Chartist movement in his novel Sybil, which served as the foundation to his "One Nation" movement.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Jews in England.
question.text: Benjamin Disraeli, the first Prime Minister of Jewish ancestry, served this nineteenth-century queen, as did his rival William Gladstone. She ruled for sixty-three years.
question.clue: After the death of her husband, Prince Albert, this ruler only ever wore black.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early radicals in British history.
swap.text: During this king's reign, the Middlesex By-Election Controversy occurred over whether to seat the radical John Wilkes. This king is more notable for having lost the American Revolutionary War.
swap.clue: During this man's reign, Spencer Perceval became the first British PM to be assassinated, and he faced the anti-Catholic Gordon Riots in his capital.

question.text: A Fellow of the Royal Horticultural Society, he organized a municipal bank in Birmingham while serving as its mayor. After serving as Chancellor for the Exchequer, he assumed the British Prime Ministry in 1937. For fifteen points, name this man who spoke with Hitler on three separate occasions, while trying to adhere to a policy of appeasement.
question.clue: Ramsay MacDonald, Stanley Baldwin, and this man were the three Prime Ministers attacked by the book Guilty Men, which was published in 1940.

swap.leadin: The namesake of these riots later was charged with libeling Marie Antoinette.
swap.text: Identify this series of riots that took place in England in 1780 in response to the passage of the Catholic Relief Act two years earlier.
swap.clue: Participants wore blue ribbons in their hats in imitation of its initiator, who was defended in court by Thomas Erskine and acquitted.

question.text: This man was the actual prime minister during the end of the Seven Years War, having formed an uneasy partnership with Pitt. A longtime Secretary of State, he served a previous stint as prime minister at the beginning of the war, only to be forced out when Britain started off slowly.

swap.leadin: Name the following prime ministers of England.
swap.text: This family had a father and son serve under George III as prime ministers, the younger of whom remains the youngest person to have served as prime minister.
swap.clue: A prime minister with this surname introduced Britain's first modern income tax and resigned over the issue of Catholic Emancipation.

question.leadin: This man persisted with using Manchurian ponies instead of stronger light or dark ones, but they all ended up dying anyway.
question.text: Name this man who ended his diary with the line "For God's sake look after our people." This man also wrote in his diary that Lawrence Oates marched to his death after saying "I am just going outside and may be some time."
question.clue: While leading an Antarctic expedition, Hillary set up a base named for this explorer, who led the Terra Nova expedition to the South Pole. Before his death, he wrote a diary entry stating "For God's sake look after our people".

swap.leadin: This law stated that the requirement to own land was to merely live in a house with a hearth sufficient to boil a pot.
swap.text: Identify this 1832 law that massively changed the English and Welsh electoral system, expanded the franchise and eliminated so-called "pocket" and "rotten boroughs".
swap.answerHtml: Representation of the People Act 1832 [Accept Great Reform Act 1832 or 1832 Reform Act or First Reform Act]

question.leadin: Description acceptable. Stale sandwiches provided by one service were a common talking point supporting this policy, which led to the creation of companies like Connex.
question.text: Identify or describe this policy in John Major's 1992 platform, which critics claim reduced safety standards and led to accidents at Southall, Ladbroke Grove, and Hatfield.
question.answerHtml: privatization of British Rail [accept answers involving turning over public rail infrastructure to private owners or companies]

swap.leadin: This organisation employed the ships Mi Amigo and Ross Revenge in its most famous endeavour, and it is the basis of a 2009 Richard Curtis film starring Philip Seymour Hoffman.
swap.text: Name this still-extant pirate radio station founded by Ronan O'Rahilly in 1964. Its infamously broadcast from international waters, initially in competition with Project Atlanta, to circumvent the BBC's radio monopoly.

question.leadin: Name these figures associated with anticlericalism in the English Reformation.
question.text: John Penry was executed in 1593 for his role in the production of the texts circulated under this pen name. They were vicious satires against bishops produced by a secret printing press.
question.clue: This pseudonymous late 16th century author who may have been John Penry or Job Throckmorton. This author's many satirical tracts attacked episcopacy in the Anglican Church.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about incorrect predictions based on the Book of Revelation in early modern Britain.
swap.text: In the 1590s, this Scottish scholar calculated from Revelation that the Apocalypse would happen either in 1688 or in 1700. This scholar introduced a multiplication technique called his namesake "bones."
swap.answerHtml: John Napier of Merchiston [or Ioannes Neper; accept Napier’s rods or Napier’s bones]

question.leadin: Anglo-Saxon commoners were required to provide services that later writers called the "three-knotted obligation" or trinoda necessitas.
question.text: The first "knot" of the obligation was to serve in this militia of freemen, whose members served in Anglo-Saxon armies alongside more experienced troops such as housecarls.
question.clue: As a British soldier, you were probably part of this corps of local militia that were raised in each burh. Along with Housecarls, they formed the bulk of the British forces at the Battle of Hastings.

swap.text: Use of the "V" sign among resistance groups was encouraged by this British organization, whose members were nicknamed the "Baker Street Irregulars" and primarily carried out sabotage operations.
swap.clue: This British organisation aided the French resistance in Operation Jedburgh and were sometimes nicknamed 'the Baker Street Irregulars' or 'Churchill's Secret Army'.
